# Fine-Tuning Team

An eval-gated fine-tuning line: the strategist decides whether to train at all, the eval engineer holds the gate, the training engineer runs it.

## How the team works

The gate is the whole design. The architect refuses to plan a training run without a baseline and a written evaluation, because most fine-tuning projects that fail were never measurable in the first place. The eval engineer builds the golden sets and the graders, calibrates the judges, and is the only member who can call a checkpoint better. The training engineer prepares the data, runs the job and exports artifacts, and reports the honest curve rather than the flattering one.

## The roster

- **Fine-Tuning Architect** (leads): Decides whether to fine-tune at all, and if so which method and base model, refusing to start without a baseline and an eval gate.
- **Fine-Tuning Eval Engineer**: Builds the golden sets and graders that decide whether a checkpoint is better, and calibrates the judges before trusting them.
- **Fine-Tuning Training Engineer**: Prepares datasets, writes and launches the training run, watches the loss curves, and exports artifacts that can be served.

## Handoffs

- Fine-Tuning Architect to Fine-Tuning Eval Engineer, when a method and a base model have been chosen.
- Fine-Tuning Eval Engineer to Fine-Tuning Training Engineer, when the baseline and the gate are established.
- Fine-Tuning Training Engineer to Fine-Tuning Eval Engineer, when a checkpoint is ready.
- Fine-Tuning Eval Engineer to Fine-Tuning Architect, when no checkpoint clears the gate.
